# LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC

> Florida limited liability company (Document No. L26000221347, founded 20 April 2026). Independent broker for used and surplus power generation equipment: gas turbines, steam turbines and generator sets, offered on behalf of their owners. Managed by Lothar Schreiner, Managing Member.

Full text with all unit data and answers: https://lks360.com/llms-full.txt

## Business
- Gas turbines: industrial and aeroderivative packages, 50 and 60 Hz, new, unused or overhauled.
- Steam turbines: generator sets for power plants and industrial cogeneration.
- Generator sets: gas and diesel, for industrial and utility projects.
- Site supervision: installation and site management for industrial plants.
- Money flow: purchase payments go directly from buyer to owner, or through a third-party escrow agent agreed between them, and never pass through accounts of LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC. Brokerage income is a commission under a written agreement, paid by bank transfer after the purchase contract is signed.
- Role: independent broker on commission. Equipment stays with its owner until the sale. The purchase contract is made between buyer and owner. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC does not take title to the equipment.
- Process: buyer requirement, offer with the owner's conditions, letter of intent and inspection, purchase contract between buyer and owner.

## Short answers
Q: What is LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC?
A: LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC is an independent broker for used and surplus gas turbines, steam turbines and generator sets, organised as a Florida limited liability company in St. Petersburg, Florida. It lists 54 units on behalf of their owners on lks360.com, screens buyers by letter of intent and lets buyer and owner sign the purchase contract directly.
Page: https://lks360.com/
Q: What does a used gas turbine broker do?
A: A used gas turbine broker brings owners of surplus turbines and buyers together, presents the technical data, screens buyers by letter of intent and coordinates inspection, while buyer and owner sign the purchase contract directly. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC is an independent broker for used gas turbines, steam turbines and generator sets, paid by a commission agreed in writing; purchase payments never pass through its accounts.
Page: https://lks360.com/used-gas-turbine-broker.html
Q: How do I sell a used gas turbine?
A: Collect the unit data (model, output, frequency, year, hours, starts, condition and documents), set your net price and offer the unit through one sales route at one price. Release serial numbers, site and full documents only to buyers who sign a letter of intent, then sign the purchase contract directly with the buyer and receive payment through escrow or an irrevocable letter of credit. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC sells used gas turbines, steam turbines and generator sets for owners without an upfront fee.
Page: https://lks360.com/how-to-sell-a-used-gas-turbine.html
Q: What is the difference between a condensing and a back pressure steam turbine?
A: A condensing steam turbine exhausts into a condenser below atmospheric pressure and turns as much steam energy as possible into electricity. A back pressure steam turbine exhausts steam at a pressure a process can still use, so it makes less power per tonne of steam but supplies heat to the plant at the same time. Extraction turbines combine both by taking process steam out at one or more stages.
Page: https://lks360.com/condensing-vs-back-pressure-steam-turbine.html
Q: Used steam turbine FAQ: condensing or back pressure, what should a buyer know?
A: A condensing steam turbine exhausts into a condenser and turns as much steam as possible into power; a back pressure steam turbine exhausts steam at a pressure a process can still use, so it delivers power and process heat at the same time. A used steam turbine is further defined by its steam data (inlet pressure, inlet temperature, flow and exhaust pressure), extraction points and generator frequency. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC lists 7 used steam turbines and steam turbine generator sets on behalf of their owners.
Page: https://lks360.com/steam-turbine-faq.html
Q: What should I know before buying a used gas turbine?
A: Start with the output you need, grid frequency (50 or 60 Hz), fuel, emission limits at the site and whether the plant runs simple or combined cycle. Then check hours, starts, overhaul records and the scope of the package. Aeroderivative gas turbines suit peaking and mobile power, heavy duty gas turbines suit continuous base load.
Page: https://lks360.com/gas-turbine-faq.html
Q: What should I know before buying a used generator set?
A: Compare generator sets at the same rating (standby, prime or continuous), then check fuel (gas, diesel or heavy fuel oil), grid frequency and running hours since the last overhaul. Medium speed engines give more output per unit, high speed engines are compact and quick to install. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC lists 13 used gas and diesel generator sets on behalf of their owners.
Page: https://lks360.com/generator-set-faq.html
Q: How do I buy a used gas turbine safely?
A: Send your requirement (output, frequency, fuel, site and timeline), compare offers by stock number, then sign a letter of intent to receive full data and inspect the unit. Sign the purchase contract directly with the owner and pay through escrow or a letter of credit, never in advance to an intermediary.
Page: https://lks360.com/buying-used-gas-turbines.html
Q: How can I sell my used turbine or generator set?
A: Give one broker an exclusive sales mandate for a limited time at your net price, so the unit is offered once, at one price, with one data set. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC presents the unit to screened buyers, keeps your name and site confidential until a letter of intent and charges no upfront fee.
Page: https://lks360.com/sell.html
Q: How does LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC work?
A: LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC lists each unit on behalf of its owner, sends buyers an offer with the owner's conditions, releases full data and inspection after a letter of intent and lets buyer and owner sign the purchase contract directly. The commission is agreed in writing; purchase payments never pass through the accounts of LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC.
Page: https://lks360.com/how-we-work.html
Q: What do the common terms in used turbine trading mean?
A: This glossary defines the terms used when buying and selling used gas turbines, steam turbines and generator sets, such as LOI, proof of funds, escrow, aeroderivative, heavy duty, combined cycle, DLE and HRSG, in one or two plain sentences each.
Page: https://lks360.com/power-generation-glossary.html

Units are offered on behalf of their owners, price on request; full data and inspection follow a letter of intent.
Page: https://lks360.com/gas-turbines.html

Page: https://lks360.com/steam-turbines.html
Q: Where can I buy a used generator set?
A: LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC (lks360.com) lists 13 used and surplus gas, diesel and heavy fuel oil generator sets, including Caterpillar, Wärtsilä, MTU, Cummins and MAN engines, each with a stock number and its own page. Units are offered on behalf of their owners, price on request; full data and inspection follow a letter of intent.
Page: https://lks360.com/generator-sets.html
Q: What is coal-to-gas heat recovery repowering?
A: Heat recovery repowering replaces the coal boiler of an existing power plant with one or more gas turbines and a heat recovery steam generator (HRSG); the gas turbine exhaust raises steam for the plant's existing steam turbine, so the coal unit becomes a combined cycle plant. It suits plants whose steam turbine, condenser, cooling system and grid connection still have decades of life left. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC lists gas turbines and gas turbine trains with HRSG for such projects on behalf of their owners.
Page: https://lks360.com/coal-to-gas-repowering.html
Q: What does a buyer need before a used gas turbine can be sold?
A: A buyer first needs model, output, frequency, year, hours, starts, condition and the scope of supply. Serial numbers, site and full documents follow a signed letter of intent, and inspection follows that.
Page: https://lks360.com/how-to-sell-a-used-gas-turbine.html
Q: What is an LOI when buying a used gas turbine?
A: A letter of intent is a signed, non-binding statement in which the buyer names the stock number, the buyer company, the end user and the site and declares the intention to buy at the stated conditions. It opens full documents and inspection; the binding purchase contract comes later, directly between buyer and owner.
Page: https://lks360.com/how-to-sell-a-used-gas-turbine.html
Q: How is a used gas turbine paid for?
A: The buyer pays the owner directly through escrow or an irrevocable letter of credit agreed between them. Purchase payments never pass through the accounts of LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC.
Page: https://lks360.com/how-to-sell-a-used-gas-turbine.html
Q: What is an LOI when buying a used gas turbine?
A: A letter of intent is a signed, non-binding statement in which the buyer names the stock number, the buyer company, the end user and the site and declares the intention to buy at the stated conditions. It opens full documents and inspection; the binding purchase contract comes later, directly between buyer and owner.
Page: https://lks360.com/buying-used-gas-turbines.html
Q: Condensing vs back pressure: which used steam turbine fits my plant?
A: If the plant needs process steam all the time, a back pressure or extraction turbine uses the steam twice, first for power and then for heat. If only electricity is needed, a condensing turbine gives more power from the same steam but needs a condenser and cooling. See condensing vs back pressure steam turbine for the full comparison.
Page: https://lks360.com/steam-turbine-faq.html
Q: Which data does a seller need from a buyer of a used steam turbine?
A: Live steam pressure and temperature, steam mass flow, the required exhaust or back pressure, extraction pressures and flows, generator frequency and the site cooling conditions.
Page: https://lks360.com/steam-turbine-faq.html

## Questions and answers per model

### Siemens SGT-800 (https://lks360.com/siemens-sgt-800-for-sale.html)
Q: Where can I buy a used Siemens SGT-800?
A: LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC (lks360.com), an independent broker based in Florida, lists 2 used or surplus Siemens SGT-800 units for sale, stock numbers LKS-GT-02, LKS-GT-03, on behalf of their owners and subject to prior sale. Price on request; full data and inspection follow a letter of intent. The purchase contract is made directly between buyer and owner.
Q: What is the Siemens SGT-800?
A: The Siemens SGT-800 is an industrial gas turbine by Siemens Energy. Output: up to 62 MW (simple cycle, 45 to 62 MW ratings). Typical applications: industrial power generation, oil and gas, combined cycle and cogeneration. Source: Siemens Energy, SGT-800 product page.
Q: What is the Siemens SGT-800 used for?
A: The SGT-800 is a Siemens Energy industrial gas turbine at the top of the industrial output range. It goes back to the GTX100 and is often installed in combined cycle and cogeneration plants. Typical uses: combined cycle power plants; industrial cogeneration and district heating; simple cycle power for industry.
Q: What was the SGT-800 called before?
A: The SGT-800 goes back to the GTX100 gas turbine developed by ABB and later Alstom, now part of Siemens Energy.
Q: Is the SGT-800 used in combined cycle?
A: Yes. Combined cycle and cogeneration are main applications. Several units listed on lks360.com are combined cycle blocks with gas turbine and steam turbine.
Q: What does a Siemens SGT-800 cost?
A: LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC quotes the price of each listed SGT-800 on request with the stock number. It depends on rating, hours and starts, overhaul records, condition, scope, combined cycle equipment, frequency and location.
Q: Who sells the Siemens SGT-800 units listed here?
A: LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC, a Florida limited liability company and independent broker, lists each unit on behalf of its owner. The purchase contract is made directly between buyer and owner.
Q: Is the Siemens SGT-800 still available?
A: Each unit is offered on behalf of its owner and subject to prior sale. Send the stock number and we confirm the current status.
Q: What does a used Siemens SGT-800 cost?
A: Send the stock number and we reply with the price. The full data sheet, documents and inspection follow your letter of intent.

### GE TM2500 (https://lks360.com/ge-tm2500-for-sale.html)
Q: Where can I buy a used GE TM2500?
A: LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC (lks360.com), an independent broker based in Florida, lists 1 used or surplus GE TM2500 unit for sale, stock number LKS-GT-38, on behalf of its owner and subject to prior sale. Price on request; full data and inspection follow a letter of intent. The purchase contract is made directly between buyer and owner.
Q: What is the GE TM2500?
A: The GE TM2500 is a mobile aeroderivative gas turbine by GE Vernova. Output: 34.5 MW net (DLE) and 34.6 MW net (SAC) at 50 Hz. Typical applications: bridge to permanent power, emergency and backup power, isolated locations. Source: GE Vernova, TM2500 product page.
Q: What is the GE TM2500 used for?
A: The GE TM2500 is a trailer mounted gas turbine generator built around the LM2500 aeroderivative engine. It is designed to be moved by road and set up quickly where power is needed. Typical uses: emergency and temporary power; grid support during plant outages; fast track power for industrial projects.
Q: What is the difference between the TM2500 and the LM2500?
A: The TM2500 is a mobile, trailer mounted package with an LM2500 family engine. The LM2500 is usually installed as a stationary package. See LM2500 vs TM2500 for the details.
Q: How fast can a TM2500 be installed?
A: The TM2500 is designed for short installation times. The real time depends on site preparation, fuel supply and grid connection.
Q: What does a used GE TM2500 cost?
A: LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC quotes the price of each listed TM2500 on request with the stock number. It depends on version, hours and cycles since overhaul, overhaul records, condition, trailers and scope, frequency and location.
Q: What is the difference between the TM2500 and the TM2500+?
A: According to GE, the TM2500+ introduced in 2008 is packaged on a two-trailer system and delivers up to 34 MW, with a 30 percent increase in power from a footprint 75 percent smaller than its predecessor.
Q: What does Gen 6 mean on a TM2500?
A: Gen 4, Gen 5 and Gen 6 are generation labels used in the market for TM2500 units. A buyer checks the stated generation against the engine and generator documents, which follow the letter of intent.
Q: Who sells the GE TM2500 units listed here?
A: LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC, a Florida limited liability company and independent broker, lists each unit on behalf of its owner. The purchase contract is made directly between buyer and owner.

### GE LM2500 (https://lks360.com/ge-lm2500-for-sale.html)

Q: What is the GE LM2500?
A: The GE LM2500 is an aeroderivative gas turbine by GE Vernova. Output: about 37 MW simple cycle (LM2500XPRESS+ G4 34.5 MW, G5 36.3 MW net, 50 Hz). Typical applications: fast power and cycling, grid support, data centers, reserve power, CHP, industrial. Source: GE Vernova, LM2500 product page.
Q: What is the GE LM2500 used for?
A: The GE LM2500 is an aeroderivative gas turbine developed from the CF6 aircraft engine. It is used in industrial power generation, on ships and in oil and gas. Typical uses: power generation and cogeneration; mechanical drive for compressors; marine propulsion and offshore power.
Q: What is the difference between the LM2500, LM2500+ and LM2500+G4?
A: They are versions of the same aeroderivative family. The LM2500+ and LM2500+G4 have higher output than the base LM2500. The data sheet of each unit states the exact version.
Q: Can an LM2500 engine be exchanged?
A: Aeroderivative engines can be removed and exchanged as a whole, which shortens outages. Engine exchange and lease options depend on the depot and are clarified case by case.
Q: What is the output of a GE LM2500?
A: GE Vernova states about 37 MW in simple cycle for the current LM2500, with 34.5 MW (G4) and 36.3 MW (G5) net at 50 Hz for the LM2500XPRESS+ package. Older units have less; the data sheet of each unit states its rating.

### GE LM6000 (https://lks360.com/ge-lm6000-for-sale.html)
Q: Where can I buy a used GE LM6000?
A: LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC (lks360.com), an independent broker based in Florida, lists 3 used or surplus GE LM6000 units for sale, stock numbers LKS-GT-19, LKS-GT-32, LKS-GT-35, on behalf of their owners and subject to prior sale. Price on request; full data and inspection follow a letter of intent. The purchase contract is made directly between buyer and owner.
Q: What is the GE LM6000?
A: The GE LM6000 is an aeroderivative gas turbine by GE Vernova. Output: about 57 MW simple cycle (51.1 MW PC Sprint, 56.9 MW PF+ Sprint net). Typical applications: fast start and grid support, backup power, flexible generation and CHP. Source: GE Vernova, LM6000 product page.
Q: What is the GE LM6000 used for?
A: The GE LM6000 is a two shaft aeroderivative gas turbine developed from the CF6-80C2 aircraft engine. It is widely used for peaking, cogeneration and fast start power plants. Typical uses: peaking plants with frequent starts; cogeneration and combined cycle; power barges and fast track plants.
Q: What does SPRINT mean on an LM6000?
A: SPRINT stands for spray intercooling. Water is sprayed into the compressor to cool the air, which raises output, mainly on hot days.
Q: What is the difference between LM6000 PA, PC and PD?
A: They are generations of the LM6000. PC and PD versions came later than the PA and differ in output and combustion system. The data sheet of each unit states the version.
Q: What does a used GE LM6000 cost?
A: LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC quotes the price of each listed LM6000 on request with the stock number. It depends on version, hours and cycles since overhaul, overhaul records, condition, scope, frequency, emission system and location.
Q: Is the wiring harness included with a used LM6000?
A: Harnesses, sensors and control cabling belong to the engine and package scope. The scope list of each unit states what is included; LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC lists complete units and packages, not single spare parts.
Q: What is the difference between LM6000 SAC and DLE?
A: SAC is the single annular combustor, which GE Vernova describes as water injected; DLE is dry low emissions combustion. GE Vernova offers the current LM6000 in both configurations, and the data sheet of a used unit states which one it has.
Q: Who sells the GE LM6000 units listed here?
A: LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC, a Florida limited liability company and independent broker, lists each unit on behalf of its owner. The purchase contract is made directly between buyer and owner.
Q: Is the GE LM6000 still available?
A: Each unit is offered on behalf of its owner and subject to prior sale. Send the stock number and we confirm the current status.
Q: What does a used GE LM6000 cost?
A: Send the stock number and we reply with the price. The full data sheet, documents and inspection follow your letter of intent.
Q: Can I inspect the unit, and how is payment made?
A: Yes. After your letter of intent you receive the technical documents and can inspect the unit. Payment goes directly from buyer to owner, or through a third-party escrow agent agreed between them.

A: The GE Frame 5 (MS5001) is a heavy duty gas turbine with one of the longest service histories in the industry. Many units still run in power plants, refineries and on power barges. Q: What is the difference between the MS5001 and the MS5002?

Q: What is the Solar Titan used for?
A: Titan is the largest gas turbine family of Solar Turbines, a Caterpillar company. The Titan 130 and Titan 250 are used for power generation and for driving compressors in oil and gas. Typical uses: gas compression on pipelines and production sites; industrial power generation and cogeneration; offshore power and mechanical drive.
Q: What is the difference between the Titan 130 and the Titan 250?

How We Work | Turbine Brokerage Process and FAQ | LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC

How does LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC work? LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC lists each unit on behalf of its owner, sends buyers an offer with the owner's conditions, releases full data and inspection after a letter of intent and lets buyer and owner sign the purchase contract directly. The commission is agreed in writing; purchase payments never pass through the accounts of LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC.

How we work

### Four clear steps

The purchase contract is made between buyer and owner. Buyers find a checklist in our buyer guide.

1

### Requirement

The buyer sends type, output, frequency, fuel and location.

2

### Offer

We match units from owners and send an offer with the owner's conditions.

3

### LOI and inspection

With a letter of intent the buyer receives full data and can inspect the unit.

4

### Contract

Buyer and owner sign the purchase contract. Our commission is agreed in writing.

Questions and answers

### Frequently asked questions

### Does LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC own the equipment?

No. We are an independent broker. The equipment belongs to its owner until the sale, and we do not take title to it.

### Who signs the purchase contract?

The buyer and the owner sign the purchase contract directly. Payment terms are agreed between them in that contract.

### How is LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC paid?

We work on commission. The commission is agreed in writing before the deal is closed and paid by bank transfer after the purchase contract is signed. Purchase payments go directly from buyer to owner, or through a third-party escrow agent agreed between them, and never pass through accounts of LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC.

### When do I receive serial numbers, location and full technical data?

After receipt of a letter of intent. Before that we send an offer with model, output, frequency, condition and the owner's conditions.

### Can I inspect the unit before buying?

Yes. After the letter of intent the buyer can inspect the unit on site. The inspection terms are agreed with the owner.

### I own a turbine. Will you publish my name or site?

No. We present the unit with its technical data only. Your name and the site location stay confidential until a buyer has signed a letter of intent and you agree.

## Page: https://lks360.com/buying-used-gas-turbines.html

Buying a Used Gas Turbine | Buyer Checklist | LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC

Buyer guide

### Buying a used gas turbine

What to ask for, what to check and how a purchase of used or surplus power generation equipment runs. The same points apply to steam turbines and generator sets.

How do I buy a used gas turbine safely? Send your requirement (output, frequency, fuel, site and timeline), compare offers by stock number, then sign a letter of intent to receive full data and inspect the unit. Sign the purchase contract directly with the owner and pay through escrow or a letter of credit, never in advance to an intermediary.

Direct answers

### What is an LOI when buying a used gas turbine?

A letter of intent is a signed, non-binding statement in which the buyer names the stock number, the buyer company, the end user and the site and declares the intention to buy at the stated conditions. It opens full documents and inspection; the binding purchase contract comes later, directly between buyer and owner.

### 1. Define the requirement

Send required output, grid frequency (50 or 60 Hz), fuel (natural gas, liquid fuel or dual fuel), emission limits at the site, simple cycle or combined cycle, delivery country and planned start of operation. With these points owners can answer with a concrete offer instead of a general list.

### 2. Ask for the right records

The value of a used turbine depends on its history. Ask for operating hours and starts, the maintenance and overhaul history, recent borescope or inspection reports, and preservation records if the unit has been stored. Missing records are not always a showstopper, but they should be reflected in the inspection scope.

### 3. Understand the condition

Unused units have not been operated after delivery. Preserved units were operated and then stored under a preservation procedure. Running units are still in service and can be inspected in operation before dismantling.

### 4. Check the scope of supply

Clarify what is included: turbine core, generator, control system, auxiliaries, fuel system, enclosure, transformers, and for combined cycle the steam turbine and heat recovery steam generator. Spare parts and documentation sets should be listed in the offer.

### 5. Letter of intent and inspection

After a letter of intent the buyer receives serial numbers, location and full technical data and can inspect the unit on site. Inspection terms are agreed with the owner. Many buyers involve an independent inspector or the original manufacturer's service.

### 6. Dismantling, transport and installation

Agree who dismantles, packs and ships the unit, and under which Incoterm. Heavy lifts and oversize transport need early planning. Recommissioning at the new site is usually a separate contract.

### 7. Compliance and contract

Buyer, owner and end use are screened against sanctions lists, and export control rules are checked before signing. The purchase contract is signed between buyer and owner. Purchase payments go directly from buyer to owner or through an escrow agent agreed between them. See compliance and how we work.

### Current units

See the inventory, or browse gas turbines, steam turbines and generator sets.

## Page: https://lks360.com/gas-turbine-faq.html

Used Gas Turbine FAQ | Aeroderivative, Heavy Duty, 50/60 Hz, LOI | LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC

Knowledge

### Used gas turbine FAQ

Plain answers to the questions buyers and owners ask about used and surplus gas turbines, steam turbines and generator sets.

What should I know before buying a used gas turbine? Start with the output you need, grid frequency (50 or 60 Hz), fuel, emission limits at the site and whether the plant runs simple or combined cycle. Then check hours, starts, overhaul records and the scope of the package. Aeroderivative gas turbines suit peaking and mobile power, heavy duty gas turbines suit continuous base load.

### What is the difference between an aeroderivative and a heavy duty gas turbine?

Aeroderivative gas turbines are derived from aircraft engines. They are compact, light, start quickly and are often used for peaking, mobile and oil and gas applications, for example the GE LM2500, LM6000 and TM2500. Heavy duty or industrial gas turbines are built for continuous base load operation and long intervals between overhauls, for example the GE Frame 6B, 7EA and 9E or the Siemens SGT5-2000E and Westinghouse 501 and 701 series.

### Which manufacturers build the gas turbines traded on the used market?

The units most often traded come from GE (GE Vernova), Siemens (Siemens Energy, including former Westinghouse and Alstom lines), Mitsubishi Power, Solar Turbines (Titan, Taurus, Centaur, Mars), Kawasaki, Ansaldo Energia and Baker Hughes (Nuovo Pignone).

### Can a 50 Hz gas turbine be used in a 60 Hz grid?

Not without changes. Generator frequency follows shaft speed, so a unit built for 50 Hz usually needs a different gearbox or generator, or a design that is specified for both frequencies. Check the generator nameplate data and ask the owner before making an offer.

### What is the difference between simple cycle and combined cycle?

In simple cycle the gas turbine drives the generator and the exhaust heat leaves through the stack. In combined cycle the exhaust heat goes into a heat recovery steam generator (HRSG), and the steam drives a steam turbine that produces additional power from the same fuel.

### What does DLE or DLN mean on a gas turbine?

DLE (dry low emissions) and DLN (dry low NOx) are combustion systems that reduce nitrogen oxide emissions without injecting water or steam. Whether a unit has DLE or DLN matters when the site has strict emission limits.

### What determines the price of a used gas turbine?

Model and output, operating hours and starts since new and since the last overhaul, condition (unused, preserved or running), the completeness of the maintenance records, the scope of supply (generator, controls, auxiliaries, HRSG, spare parts), frequency and fuel options, and the cost and effort of dismantling and transport from its location.

### Which documents should a buyer ask for?

Operating hours and starts, the maintenance and overhaul history, recent borescope or inspection reports, preservation records for stored units, the scope of supply list and generator data. Full documents are normally released after a letter of intent.

### What is an LOI in an equipment purchase?

A letter of intent is a written statement from the buyer that names the unit, the price offered, the buyer company, the end user and country of installation and the intended payment route. It is the step that releases full data and inspection. See the LOI step in the buyer guide.

### What is proof of funds (POF)?

Proof of funds is a bank letter confirming that the buyer can pay the purchase price. It is usually requested before contract or inspection, not with the first enquiry.

### How is a used turbine paid safely?

Through an escrow agent or an irrevocable letter of credit agreed between buyer and owner. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC never receives purchase payments.

### Gas engine generator set or gas turbine: which fits better?

Gas engine generator sets (for example Caterpillar, Wartsila, MTU, MAN or Jenbacher) suit smaller and modular plants and keep high efficiency at part load. Gas turbines suit larger outputs, combined cycle plants and sites that need high power density. The decision depends on output, load profile, fuel, emissions and site.

### Where can I buy a used gas turbine?

Used gas turbines are sold by their owners directly, through brokers and through equipment marketplaces. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC is an independent broker and lists units on behalf of their owners at lks360.com/inventory.html, with model pages for each turbine type.

### How do I sell a used or surplus gas turbine?

Collect model, year, hours, condition, scope and your price idea, then offer the unit through one broker with an exclusive mandate or through several channels. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC offers owners an exclusive sales mandate with one price in the market, screened buyers and no upfront fee: lks360.com/sell.html

## Page: https://lks360.com/steam-turbine-faq.html

Used Steam Turbine FAQ | Condensing, Back Pressure, Extraction | LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC

Knowledge

### Used steam turbine FAQ

Plain answers to the questions buyers and owners ask about used and surplus steam turbines and steam turbine generator sets.

Used steam turbine FAQ: condensing or back pressure, what should a buyer know? A condensing steam turbine exhausts into a condenser and turns as much steam as possible into power; a back pressure steam turbine exhausts steam at a pressure a process can still use, so it delivers power and process heat at the same time. A used steam turbine is further defined by its steam data (inlet pressure, inlet temperature, flow and exhaust pressure), extraction points and generator frequency. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC lists 7 used steam turbines and steam turbine generator sets on behalf of their owners.

Direct answers

### Condensing vs back pressure: which used steam turbine fits my plant?

If the plant needs process steam all the time, a back pressure or extraction turbine uses the steam twice, first for power and then for heat. If only electricity is needed, a condensing turbine gives more power from the same steam but needs a condenser and cooling. See condensing vs back pressure steam turbine for the full comparison.

### Which data does a seller need from a buyer of a used steam turbine?

Live steam pressure and temperature, steam mass flow, the required exhaust or back pressure, extraction pressures and flows, generator frequency and the site cooling conditions.

### What types of steam turbines are traded on the used market?

Condensing turbines exhaust into a condenser and turn as much steam energy as possible into power. Back pressure turbines exhaust steam at a pressure that a process can still use, for example in a paper mill, refinery or sugar factory. Extraction turbines take steam out at one or more stages for process heat and send the rest on to the exhaust.

### Which manufacturers build the steam turbines sold used?

Units most often traded come from Siemens Energy (SST series), GE Vernova (including former Alstom lines), Mitsubishi Power, Doosan Skoda, MAN Energy Solutions, Elliott, Dresser Rand, Shin Nippon and Triveni.

### Which data define a steam turbine for a new site?

Live steam pressure and temperature, steam mass flow, exhaust or back pressure, extraction pressures and flows, output, speed and generator frequency. A used turbine fits a new site only when these values match the boiler or heat recovery steam generator there, so buyers send their steam data first.

### Can a steam turbine be added to an existing gas turbine?

Yes. With a heat recovery steam generator behind the gas turbine, the exhaust heat makes steam that drives a steam turbine. This turns a simple cycle plant into a combined cycle plant and produces additional power from the same fuel.

### What is a steam turbine generator set?

A package of steam turbine, gearbox where needed, generator, lube oil system and controls on a common base or in a common scope. Buying the complete set saves engineering, because the parts are already matched.

### Which documents should a buyer ask for?

Heat balance and design steam data, operating hours and starts, the overhaul and inspection history, rotor and blade inspection reports, preservation records for stored units, the scope of supply list and generator data. Full documents are normally released after a letter of intent.

### Is a used steam turbine worth it compared with a new one?

A used or surplus turbine is usually available much sooner than a new build and costs less. It is a good choice when its design data fit the site and the documents show a sound maintenance history. A site visit or third party inspection before contract confirms the condition.

### How is a used steam turbine bought and paid?

The buyer sends a letter of intent, receives the full data and inspects the unit, then signs the purchase contract with the owner. Payment runs through an escrow agent or an irrevocable letter of credit. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC never receives purchase payments.

### Where can I buy a used steam turbine?

LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC is an independent broker and lists steam turbines and steam turbine generator sets on behalf of their owners at lks360.com/steam-turbines.html

### How do I sell a used steam turbine?

Collect model, year, steam data, output, hours, condition, scope and your price idea. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC offers owners an exclusive sales mandate with one price in the market, screened buyers and no upfront fee: lks360.com/sell.html

## Page: https://lks360.com/generator-set-faq.html

Used Generator Set FAQ | Gas and Diesel Gensets, Prime and Standby | LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC

Knowledge

### Used generator set FAQ

Plain answers to the questions buyers and owners ask about used and surplus gas and diesel generator sets and engine power plants.

What should I know before buying a used generator set? Compare generator sets at the same rating (standby, prime or continuous), then check fuel (gas, diesel or heavy fuel oil), grid frequency and running hours since the last overhaul. Medium speed engines give more output per unit, high speed engines are compact and quick to install. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC lists 13 used gas and diesel generator sets on behalf of their owners.

### What is the difference between prime, continuous and standby rating?

Standby rating is for emergency use when the grid fails, with limited running hours per year. Prime rating allows unlimited hours at variable load. Continuous rating allows unlimited hours at constant full load. Always compare generator sets at the same rating, because the same set has a different kW value for each.

### Gas engine or diesel generator set: which fits better?

Gas engine sets suit continuous operation where pipeline gas, biogas or associated gas is available, and they produce lower emissions. Diesel sets start fast and run on stored fuel, so they are common for standby, remote sites and islands. The choice depends on fuel, running hours, emissions and site.

### What is the difference between high speed and medium speed engines?

High speed engines, for example the Caterpillar 3516, MTU 4000 series or Cummins QSK, are compact and quick to install. Medium speed engines, for example the Wartsila 34SG, MAN 32/40 or Caterpillar G20CM34, are larger and heavier, run at lower speed and are built for long continuous operation in power plants.

### Can a 50 Hz generator set be used in a 60 Hz grid?

Usually only after changes. Engine speed and generator are matched to one frequency, so a 50 Hz set often needs a different generator or speed setting, and the output changes. Check the nameplate data and ask the owner before making an offer.

### Which manufacturers build the generator sets traded used?

Common makes are Caterpillar, Cummins, MTU (Rolls Royce Power Systems), Wartsila, MAN Energy Solutions, INNIO Jenbacher, MWM, Kohler and Perkins.

### Which documents should a buyer ask for?

Running hours, the overhaul history with dates and hours, oil analysis reports, load test records, the scope of supply (engine, generator, switchgear, radiators, controls, container) and the generator data. Full documents are normally released after a letter of intent.

### What determines the price of a used generator set?

Make and model, output and rating, running hours since new and since the last overhaul, condition, scope of supply, fuel and frequency, emission equipment, and the cost of dismantling and transport from its location.

### How is a used generator set bought and paid?

The buyer sends a letter of intent, receives the full data and inspects the set, then signs the purchase contract with the owner. Payment runs through an escrow agent or an irrevocable letter of credit. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC never receives purchase payments.

### Where can I buy a used generator set?

LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC is an independent broker and lists gas and diesel generator sets on behalf of their owners at lks360.com/generator-sets.html

### How do I sell a used generator set or engine power plant?

Collect make, model, output, hours, condition, scope and your price idea. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC offers owners an exclusive sales mandate with one price in the market, screened buyers and no upfront fee: lks360.com/sell.html

## Page: https://lks360.com/power-generation-glossary.html

Power Generation Equipment Glossary | Gas Turbine, Steam Turbine, Genset Terms | LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC

Knowledge

### Power generation equipment glossary

Short definitions of the terms used when buying and selling used gas turbines, steam turbines and generator sets.

What do the common terms in used turbine trading mean? This glossary defines the terms used when buying and selling used gas turbines, steam turbines and generator sets, such as LOI, proof of funds, escrow, aeroderivative, heavy duty, combined cycle, DLE and HRSG, in one or two plain sentences each.

 Aeroderivative gas turbine
 A gas turbine derived from an aircraft engine, light and quick to start, for example the GE LM2500 and LM6000.
 Heavy duty gas turbine
 An industrial gas turbine built for continuous operation and long overhaul intervals, for example the GE Frame 9E or Siemens Westinghouse W501.
 ISO rating
 The output and efficiency of a gas turbine at standard conditions of 15 degrees Celsius, sea level and 60 percent relative humidity. Real output falls at higher ambient temperature and altitude.
 Heat rate
 The fuel energy needed to produce one unit of electricity, for example in kJ per kWh or Btu per kWh. A lower heat rate means higher efficiency.
 Simple cycle
 A plant where the gas turbine drives the generator and the exhaust heat leaves through the stack.
 Combined cycle (CCGT, CCPP)
 A plant where the exhaust heat of the gas turbine makes steam in a heat recovery steam generator and the steam drives a steam turbine for additional power.
 HRSG
 Heat recovery steam generator. The boiler behind a gas turbine that uses its exhaust heat to make steam.
 DLE and DLN
 Dry low emissions and dry low NOx. Combustion systems that cut nitrogen oxide emissions without water or steam injection.
 Dual fuel
 A turbine or engine that can run on two fuels, usually natural gas and diesel or light fuel oil.
 Hot gas path inspection
 A scheduled inspection of the combustion and turbine parts exposed to the hottest gas.
 Major overhaul
 The largest scheduled maintenance event, where the turbine or engine is opened completely and worn parts are replaced. Hours since the last major overhaul are a key value for buyers.
 Borescope inspection
 An inspection of the inside of a turbine or engine through small ports with an optical probe, without opening the casing.
 Equivalent operating hours (EOH)
 A count that adds operating hours and a weighting for starts, trips and fuel, used by some manufacturers to plan maintenance.
 Preservation
 Measures that protect a stored unit against corrosion, for example dry air, desiccant and sealed packaging. Buyers of stored units ask for the preservation records.
 Condensing steam turbine
 A steam turbine that exhausts into a condenser to produce as much power as possible.
 Back pressure steam turbine
 A steam turbine that exhausts at a pressure a process can still use for heat.
 Prime, continuous and standby rating
 Generator set ratings for unlimited variable load, unlimited constant load and limited emergency use.
 Power barge
 A floating power plant on a barge or ship hull, often with gas turbines or engines, that can be moved to a new site.
 LOI
 Letter of intent. A written statement by the buyer naming the unit, offered price, buyer company, end user, country of installation and payment route. It releases full data and inspection.
 POF
 Proof of funds. A bank letter confirming that the buyer can pay the purchase price.
 NCNDA
 Non circumvention and non disclosure agreement between the parties of a deal.
 Escrow
 A neutral third party that holds the purchase payment until the agreed conditions, for example delivery or transfer of title, are met.
 Letter of credit (L/C)
 A bank undertaking to pay the seller when the documents named in the credit are presented.
 Incoterms (EXW, FOB, CIF, DAP)
 Standard trade terms of the International Chamber of Commerce that define where risk and cost pass from seller to buyer.
 Exclusive sales mandate
 An agreement where an owner gives one broker the sole right to market a unit, so the unit appears with one price and one contact in the market.

More detail: buyer guide, gas turbine FAQ, steam turbine FAQ, generator set FAQ, glossary, how we work, inventory.

## Page: https://lks360.com/how-to-sell-a-used-gas-turbine.html

How to Sell a Used Gas Turbine | Step by Step Guide for Owners | LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC

Knowledge

### How do I sell a used gas turbine?

A step by step guide for owners of used and surplus gas turbines.

How do I sell a used gas turbine? Collect the unit data (model, output, frequency, year, hours, starts, condition and documents), set your net price and offer the unit through one sales route at one price. Release serial numbers, site and full documents only to buyers who sign a letter of intent, then sign the purchase contract directly with the buyer and receive payment through escrow or an irrevocable letter of credit. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC sells used gas turbines, steam turbines and generator sets for owners without an upfront fee.

Direct answers

### What does a buyer need before a used gas turbine can be sold?

A buyer first needs model, output, frequency, year, hours, starts, condition and the scope of supply. Serial numbers, site and full documents follow a signed letter of intent, and inspection follows that.

### What is an LOI when buying a used gas turbine?

A letter of intent is a signed, non-binding statement in which the buyer names the stock number, the buyer company, the end user and the site and declares the intention to buy at the stated conditions. It opens full documents and inspection; the binding purchase contract comes later, directly between buyer and owner.

### How is a used gas turbine paid for?

The buyer pays the owner directly through escrow or an irrevocable letter of credit agreed between them. Purchase payments never pass through the accounts of LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC.

Short answer: Collect the unit data, set your net price, offer the unit through one sales route at one price, release full data only to buyers who sign a letter of intent, sign the purchase contract directly with the buyer and receive payment through escrow or an irrevocable letter of credit. The same steps apply to steam turbines and generator sets.

### Step by step

Collect the unit data. Manufacturer and model, output, year, operating hours since new and since the last overhaul, frequency, fuel, condition, scope of supply (generator, HRSG, balance of plant, spare parts) and the documents and photos you have.

Set your net price. Decide the amount you want to receive for the unit as it stands, and whether dismantling, loading and transport are included or are for the buyer.

Choose one sales route. You can sell directly, through a dealer who buys the unit, or through a broker. If several brokers offer the same unit at different prices, buyers see it everywhere and the price drops. One exclusive mandate keeps one price and one data set in the market.

Screen buyers. Give price and key data first. Release serial numbers, site, full documents and inspection only after a signed letter of intent and with your consent.

Inspection and contract. The buyer inspects the unit on site under terms you agree. Buyer and owner sign the purchase contract directly.

Payment and handover. The purchase price is paid through an escrow agent or an irrevocable letter of credit before the unit leaves the site.

### Which data does a buyer need first?

Model, output, year, operating hours since new and since the last overhaul, frequency, fuel, condition, scope of supply and the region of the site. Serial numbers and the exact site follow after a letter of intent.

### Should I give my turbine to several brokers?

It usually lowers the price. The same unit then appears at different prices with different data, and serious buyers start to doubt it. An exclusive mandate for a fixed period gives one offer, one price and one consistent data set.

### Do I pay anything in advance to sell through LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC?

No. There is no upfront fee. Our income is agreed in writing and only arises when the unit is sold. Details: exclusive sales mandate

### Will my company name and site be published?

No. The unit is presented with its technical data and a stock number only. Name and site stay confidential until a buyer has signed a letter of intent and you agree.

### How is the purchase price paid to the owner?

Through escrow or an irrevocable letter of credit agreed in the purchase contract. Purchase payments never pass through accounts of LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC.

### Can I sell a steam turbine or generator set the same way?

Yes. The steps are the same for steam turbines, generator sets and complete power plants. Send the unit data at exclusive sales mandate

### Broker for used gas turbines and generator sets

What a broker for used turbines and generator sets does, and how to check one.

What does a used gas turbine broker do? A used gas turbine broker brings owners of surplus turbines and buyers together, presents the technical data, screens buyers by letter of intent and coordinates inspection, while buyer and owner sign the purchase contract directly. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC is an independent broker for used gas turbines, steam turbines and generator sets, paid by a commission agreed in writing; purchase payments never pass through its accounts.

Short answer: A broker for used gas turbines and generator sets brings owners of surplus equipment and buyers together, presents the technical data, screens buyers by letter of intent, coordinates inspection and lets buyer and owner sign the purchase contract directly. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC is an independent broker that lists gas turbines, steam turbines and generator sets on behalf of their owners.

### What does a turbine broker do?

Collects and checks the unit data from the owner, gives each unit a stock number, sends offers to matching buyers, receives the letter of intent, arranges full data and inspection, and supports buyer and owner until the purchase contract is signed.

### Does the broker own the equipment?

Not at LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC. The equipment belongs to its owner until the sale, and the broker does not take title to it.

### How do I check a broker before I send an LOI?

Ask for the company registration, a written fee agreement, a clear statement of who signs the purchase contract and how the purchase price is paid. A reliable broker confirms availability with the owner before every offer and never asks the buyer to pay the purchase price to the broker.

### What are warning signs in the used turbine market?

Requests for advance fees or deposits to the broker, long chains of intermediaries who have never seen the unit, the same unit offered at many different prices, refusal to allow an inspection, and payment instructions that change during the deal.

### How is LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC paid?

By commission agreed in writing before the deal is closed. Purchase payments go from buyer to owner, or through an escrow agent or letter of credit agreed between them, and never pass through accounts of LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC. More: how we work

## Page: https://lks360.com/condensing-vs-back-pressure-steam-turbine.html

Condensing vs Back Pressure Steam Turbine | Differences and Uses | LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC

Knowledge

### Condensing vs back pressure steam turbine

How condensing and back pressure steam turbines differ, and which one fits a site.

What is the difference between a condensing and a back pressure steam turbine? A condensing steam turbine exhausts into a condenser below atmospheric pressure and turns as much steam energy as possible into electricity. A back pressure steam turbine exhausts steam at a pressure a process can still use, so it makes less power per tonne of steam but supplies heat to the plant at the same time. Extraction turbines combine both by taking process steam out at one or more stages.

Short answer: A condensing steam turbine exhausts into a condenser below atmospheric pressure and turns as much steam energy as possible into electricity. A back pressure steam turbine exhausts steam at a pressure a process can still use, so it produces less power per tonne of steam but supplies heat to the plant at the same time. Extraction turbines combine both by taking process steam out at one or more stages.

 Condensing turbineBack pressure turbine

 ExhaustInto a condenser, below atmospheric pressureAt a process pressure above atmospheric
 Main productElectricityProcess steam and electricity
 Power per tonne of steamHigherLower
 Cooling systemNeeds condenser and cooling water or air coolingNo condenser for the exhaust steam
 Typical sitesPower plants, combined cycle plants, waste to energyPaper mills, refineries, chemical plants, sugar and palm oil mills
 Runs best whenPower demand is high and heat has no useThe site needs steam all the time

### Which one should I choose for my site?

If the site needs process steam continuously, a back pressure or extraction turbine uses the steam twice, first for power and then for heat. If only electricity is needed, a condensing turbine gives more power from the same steam.

### What is an extraction condensing turbine?

A condensing turbine that also takes steam out at one or more stages for process heat. It can follow changing heat and power demand.

### Can a used back pressure turbine be converted to condensing?

Usually not in a simple way. Blading, exhaust casing and the steam path are designed for the original exhaust pressure. Choose the type that matches the site from the start.

### Which data does a seller need from a buyer?

Live steam pressure and temperature, steam mass flow, the required exhaust or back pressure, extraction pressures and flows, generator frequency and the site cooling conditions. A used turbine fits only when these values match the boiler and the process.

### Where can I buy a used condensing or back pressure steam turbine?

LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC lists used steam turbines and steam turbine generator sets on behalf of their owners: steam turbines. More answers in the steam turbine FAQ

Coal-to-Gas Repowering: Gas Turbines and HRSG for an Existing Steam Turbine | LKS 360

Home / Gas turbines / Coal-to-gas repowering

Knowledge

### Coal-to-gas repowering: gas turbines and HRSG for an existing steam turbine

How heat recovery repowering turns a coal unit into a combined cycle plant, when it pays and which gas turbines fit.

What is coal-to-gas heat recovery repowering? Heat recovery repowering replaces the coal boiler of an existing power plant with one or more gas turbines and a heat recovery steam generator (HRSG); the gas turbine exhaust raises steam for the plant's existing steam turbine, so the coal unit becomes a combined cycle plant. It suits plants whose steam turbine, condenser, cooling system and grid connection still have decades of life left. LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC lists gas turbines and gas turbine trains with HRSG for such projects on behalf of their owners.

### What is heat recovery repowering?

In heat recovery repowering the coal boiler of an existing power plant is taken out of service and replaced by one or more gas turbines with a heat recovery steam generator (HRSG). The gas turbines produce power directly, and their hot exhaust raises steam in the HRSG for the plant's existing steam turbine. The coal unit becomes a combined cycle plant that keeps its steam turbine, condenser, cooling system, switchyard and grid connection.

### When does it pay?

Condition of the steam turbine and balance of plant: the steam turbine, condenser, cooling system and transmission connection have to be good for several more decades. According to Burns & McDonnell (April 2020), keeping the existing steam turbine essentially eliminates a third of the cost of a brand-new build if the equipment is in good working condition.

Existing site: a coal plant already has interconnection, transmission, water and industrial land. According to POWER magazine (September 2026), a retiring generator's interconnection rights can often transfer to a replacement resource, usually within a window of about a year.

Proven approach: the same POWER article states that from 2011 to 2019 more than 100 coal plants were converted to or replaced by gas.

Reference: according to Siemens Energy, Cooperative Energy replaced an existing coal-fired unit at the R.D. Morrow, Sr. Generating Station in Mississippi (coal station built in 1978) with an SGT6-9000HL gas turbine that works together with the plant's existing steam turbine. The plant delivers 550 MW, and Siemens Energy states a carbon footprint reduced by 50 percent compared with the coal unit.

### The main difficulty: matching gas turbine and steam turbine

The steam an HRSG can raise follows from the exhaust flow and exhaust temperature of the gas turbine. It has to fit the design steam flow, live steam pressure and temperature, and any reheat of the existing steam turbine. If the gas turbine is too small, the steam turbine runs at part load; if it is too large, steam has to be bypassed or the gas turbine runs below its rating. The usual tools are:

the size and number of gas turbines,

supplementary firing in the HRSG,

the pressure levels and a reheat section of the HRSG to suit the steam turbine,

the space available where the coal boiler stood.

The basis for sizing is the heat balance of the steam turbine and the exhaust data of the gas turbine at site conditions, checked by the buyer's engineer.

### Grid frequency: 50 Hz or 60 Hz

The gas turbine generator has to match the grid. A plant on a 60 Hz grid, as in North America, needs a 60 Hz gas turbine generator set or one rated for both frequencies. A plant on a 50 Hz grid, as in Europe and large parts of Asia, needs a 50 Hz unit. A geared gas turbine can sometimes be adapted with a different gearbox; a large direct drive gas turbine runs at grid speed and stays on its frequency. See also used 60 Hz units for the Americas.

### What a buyer should prepare

Heat balance and design data of the existing steam turbine: steam flow, live steam and reheat pressure and temperature, extraction points, exhaust pressure.

Condition reports of steam turbine, generator, condenser and cooling system.

Grid frequency, voltage and the export capacity of the existing connection.

Fuel gas supply, emission limits and the permit route for the site.

Space where the coal boiler stood, for gas turbines and HRSG.

### Frequent questions

### Can an existing coal plant steam turbine be driven by gas turbines?

Yes. In heat recovery repowering the coal boiler is replaced by one or more gas turbines and a heat recovery steam generator, which raises steam for the existing steam turbine. The steam turbine, condenser and cooling system have to be in good condition, and the HRSG steam data have to match the steam turbine.

### How much does reusing the steam turbine save?

According to Burns & McDonnell (2020), keeping the existing steam turbine essentially eliminates a third of the cost of a brand-new build, provided the equipment is in good working condition. The actual saving depends on the condition of the steam turbine, the condenser, the cooling system and the grid connection.

### Has heat recovery repowering of a coal unit been done?

Yes. According to Siemens Energy, Cooperative Energy replaced an existing coal-fired unit at the R.D. Morrow, Sr. Generating Station in Mississippi, built in 1978, with an SGT6-9000HL gas turbine working together with the plant's existing steam turbine; the plant delivers 550 MW.

### What is the main technical difficulty?

Matching the gas turbine to the steam turbine. The steam an HRSG can raise follows from the exhaust flow and temperature of the gas turbine, and it has to fit the design steam flow, pressure and temperature of the existing steam turbine. The usual tools are the choice of gas turbine size and number, supplementary firing in the HRSG and the HRSG pressure levels.

### Does the gas turbine have to match the grid frequency?

Yes. A plant on a 60 Hz grid, as in North America, needs a 60 Hz gas turbine generator set or one rated for both frequencies. A plant on a 50 Hz grid, as in Europe and large parts of Asia, needs a 50 Hz unit.

### Which gas turbines does LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC list for repowering projects?

For 50 Hz and 60 Hz: LKS-GT-02 Siemens SGT-800 (new, 50/60 Hz). For 50 Hz: LKS-GT-25 Siemens SGT-700 gas turbine train with dual-pressure HRSG, steam turbine not included; LKS-GT-30 GE Frame 9E; LKS-GT-36 two GE Frame 9E units. Each unit is offered on behalf of its owner, price on request.

## Page: https://lks360.com/compliance.html

Compliance Policy | LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC

Compliance

### Compliance policy

### Our role

LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC is an independent broker for used and surplus power generation equipment. We do not buy, own or resell equipment. The equipment stays with its owner until the sale, and the purchase contract is made directly between buyer and owner.

### Money flow

Purchase payments go directly from buyer to owner, or through a third-party escrow agent agreed between them, and never pass through accounts of LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC. Brokerage income is a commission under a written agreement, paid by bank transfer after the purchase contract is signed. We do not accept cash, crypto assets or payments from third parties who are not party to the agreement.

### Know your counterparty

Before we send an offer with full data, we identify the buyer and the owner: company name, registration, address, authorised signatory and beneficial owner. We keep these records for the duration of the business relationship and the legal retention periods.

### Red flags

We stop a transaction if a party refuses to identify itself, asks to route payments through us or through unrelated third parties, or asks to change the stated end user or destination.

### Contact

Questions about this policy: manager@lks360.com

Gas turbines, steam turbines, generator sets and complete plants. We present your unit to buyers with its technical data. Your name and site stay confidential.

Exclusive sales mandate

### One unit, one offer, one price

Owners who want a clean sale give us an exclusive mandate for a fixed period. Your unit is then offered once, at one price, with one consistent data set, instead of appearing at different prices with several brokers.

### Why give one broker an exclusive mandate for a used turbine?

When several brokers offer the same unit at different prices, buyers see it everywhere and the price drops. With one exclusive mandate the unit is offered once, at one price, with one consistent data set.

### How long is an exclusive sales mandate?

A fixed period agreed in writing, typically 60 days, which can be extended by both sides.

### Does the owner pay anything in advance?

No. There is no upfront fee. Our income is agreed in writing and only arises when the unit is sold.

### How are buyers screened?

Buyers receive the price and key data first. Full data, photos and inspection follow only after a signed letter of intent and with the owner's consent.

### How is the purchase price paid?

Through escrow or an irrevocable letter of credit. Purchase payments never pass through accounts of LKS 360-SCHREINER LLC.
